newsitem.title: USA: Olympic Q1 reflects gross margin pressure.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Q1 reflects gross margin pressure.

text.p: Olympic Steel Inc said Thursday that its first quarter financial results reflected the gross margin pressures that affected the steel service center industry during the period.
Steady domestic demand, coupled with relatively high inventory levels from the influx of imports during late 1996, led to the gross margin pressures during the quarter, it said.

"Our financial results reflect these conditions, as we achieved record sales, offset by a reduction in our gross margin, as price increases were not able to be fully passed through to customers," said Michael D. Siegal, Olympic Steel's chief executive officer.

"The company continues to focus on potential acquisition candidates for 1997 and continues to evaluate making an investment in a new temper mill and plate processing facility in the Midstates Region and developing a more significant presence in the Southeast Region of the country," he said.

Olympic, a leading national specialized steel service center that processes and distributes flat-rolled carbon and stainless steel products, said that for the first quarter of 1997, its tonnage sold increased 7.3 percent and net sales increased 4.8 percent to $149.5 million from $142.6 million. On a per day basis, tons sold and net sales actually increased 10.7 percent and 8.2 percent, respectively, as the current year quarter had 62 shipping days compared to 64 shipping days last year.
Earnings totaled $2.4 million, or $.23 per share, compared to $3.3 million, or $.38 per share for last year's first quarter, it said.
